transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Okonkwo, thank you for sitting down with me and your son. I asked to meet because I need to discuss what happened during your procedure today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am still feeling quite shaken. My son told me you wanted to speak.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I want to be very direct with you. While I was repairing the cut on your arm, I did not provide enough numbing medication to the area. Because I didn't check in with you about your pain levels during the stitches, I performed the repair while you were experiencing significant pain.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I felt it. I felt every single stitch. I thought perhaps it was just part of the process, but it was agonizing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It should not have been. I made a mistake by not confirming that the anaesthetic had worked before I started. Does that make sense, or can I clarify any part of that for you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It makes sense. I just don't understand how someone can just keep sewing while a man is in pain.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am truly sorry, Mr. Okonkwo. I take full responsibility for this. It was my job to ensure you were comfortable and safe, and I failed to do that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My son is worried about the wound, but I am worried about something else. I am a leader in my community. People look to me. If word gets out that I was treated with such... such disregard, it reflects poorly on my family's standing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: This is a very heavy thing to carry. It sounds like you're worried that this experience might affect how your community perceives your strength or your position.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Precisely. A man of my standing should not be seen as a victim of a mistake in a hospital. It is embarrassing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you. It is a deeply distressing situation to feel that your dignity was compromised.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I appreciate you saying that. My son, do you think the wound is okay?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know, Father. Doctor, why did this happen? Were you rushing?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I was not rushing, but I was not as attentive as I should have been to your physical response. I focused on the technical part of the repair and ignored the most important part, which was your pain. I want to be clear that this was my error. Do you have any other questions about why this occurred?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I suppose I understand. But now I am just sitting here with a sore arm and a lot of anger.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize that an apology doesn't take away the pain you felt today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It doesn't. So what happens now? How do we make sure this doesn't happen to the next person?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll put a note in the file.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A note? That is it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will just keep an eye on the healing process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I expected a more detailed explanation of the recovery. Do I need special medication? Should I come back?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I think you'll be fine. Just keep it clean.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My son is asking about a follow-up appointment. When will that be?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not entirely sure yet. We'll see how the arm looks in a few days.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is very vague. I cannot tell my family that we are just waiting to see.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will check with the attending physician and we can probably figure something out soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Soon is not a date, Doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I just need to see where the schedule stands. We can touch base later.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish all turns, never interrupts, and remains regulated despite the patient's frustration regarding the follow-up plan.

E.justification: The error (insufficient numbing/failure to check pain) is named in the second turn, lay language is used, and comprehension is checked twice ('Does that make sense', 'Do you have any other questions').

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language ('I am truly sorry'), takes full personal responsibility ('I take full responsibility', 'this was my error'), and does not deflect.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions and concerns twice ('worried that this experience might affect how your community perceives your strength', 'distressing situation to feel that your dignity was compromised').

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders and vague responses ('put a note in the file', 'we'll see', 'figure something out soon') without timelines or specific next steps.
